headline: Climate change puts a 374 million euro bill on Spanish agriculture as US tariffs threaten olive oil and canned goods
summary: Climate change puts a €374 million cost on Spanish agriculture, while US tariffs threaten olive oil and canned goods. Seville, Málaga and Córdoba carry the greatest tariff risk.
why: Spain is a major olive oil and food exporter, so tariffs and climate-related losses affect farm incomes, export revenue and regional economies.
